## Break!

## Reading Questions

> - We can exchange forms of capital for goods, services, or for other kinds of capital.
> - What's an example of exchanging cultural capital for social capital and vice versa?
> - What's an example of exchanging social capital for economic capital and vice versa?
> - What's an example of exchanging economic capital for cultural capital and vice versa?

## Criticism

> - What aspects of the concept of capital and social capital ring true to you? What feels like it is missing from this theory?

## Discussion Questions

> - How can we tell when a weak tie is actually providing valuable new information versus when it is simply a less meaningful connection?
> - How has the rise of social media changed the way social capital is built compared with traditional face-to-face networks?

## Discussion Questions

> - Granovetter states that stronger ties mean more time commitment, but I feel like some people I don't spend a lot of time with, I have stronger relationships than some of the people I do spend a lot time with. How does this work?
> - Do you think that people who are well connected with other well connected people are the exception of the argument that weak ties = greater opportunities?

## Discussion Questions

> - If weak ties are so important for opportunities, but disadvantaged groups have less access to valuable networks, what could schools, workplaces, or communities do to help people build ties across different social groups? 
> - If people are becoming less involved in traditional community organizations, could online communities eventually provide the same type of social capital, trust, and connection that Putnam argues has declined?
> - Do more people on average build connections for opportunities, or build connections for social reasons and happen to find opportunities?
